text:
maya: FYI canary for the gpu-nodepool rolling upgrade in us-west-2 just failed during the helm/terraform pipeline. Pods with nodeAffinity are stuck Pending.

sam: ugh. any obvious events?

maya: kubectl describe shows:
```
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  7s (x12 over 3m)  default-scheduler  0/6 nodes are available: 6 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 4 Insufficient intel.com/eni-ips, 2 node(s) didn't match nodeAffinity.
```

jon: ENI pressure + affinity mismatch is a rough combo. Did the upgrade change the CNI chart or instance types?

maya: terraform applied a node_group update to use mixed-instance-policy (g4dn.xlarge + g5.xlarge) and the canary batch got the new launch template that includes affinity labels for `workload=gpu-training`. Helm chart for aws-cni was bumped from 1.3.2 -> 1.4.0 in the same pipeline.

priya: timeline wise, which ran first? helm or tf?

maya: pipeline runs: 1) helm chart upgrade (cni) to 1.4.0 2) terraform plan/apply nodegroup update -> canary 3) gitops reconcile for workloads. So CNI upgrade landed before new nodes came up.

rachel: 1.4.0 has the new eniPool allocation mode turned on by default. That increases IP reuse but also changes how secondary ENIs are attached. We saw subtle race conditions last year.

sam: do we have kubelet or cni logs from a failing node?

maya: from one canary node: 
```
Mar 12 10:02:41 kubelet[...]: E03012 10:02:41.123456 kubelet_node_status.go:99] Failed to update node status: "failed to allocate podIP: no available addresses in subnet for interface attach"
Mar 12 10:02:42 aws-node[...]: E03012 10:02:42.654321 eni_manager.go:211] attach failed: ENI capacity exhausted for instance g4dn.xlarge-abc123
```

jon: that explains Insufficient ENIs. Mixed-instance policy might pick instance types with lower eni count per instance. g4dn.xlarge has fewer IPv4 addresses than g5.xlarge. The affinity label on new nodes means pods prefer those nodes but IP capacity is lower.

priya: quick mitigation: rollback the CNI chart to 1.3.2 and pause the tf rollout? Or scale the subnet pool?

sam: also can patch the nodeAffinity temporarily to be soft (preferredDuringScheduling) for the canary set, to let pods schedule elsewhere while we fix ENIs. But that requires a quick replicas/patch change in gitops which is messy mid-rollout.

maya: infra-bot: rollback helm release?

infra-bot: Received request to rollback release `aws-cni` in cluster `us-west-2` to v1.3.2. Confirm with `yes` to proceed.

rachel: before we rollback, can we check if increasing `podDensity` or changing `eniPool` settings in 1.4.0 would be less disruptive? 1.4.0 supports `eniPool.maxAttachableENIs` but it's gated in our config.

sam: we need a quick stopgap. If we pause the terraform canary, we should avoid hitting more nodes with lower ENI counts. maya, can you abort the pipeline?

maya: aborted the terraform canary job. Pipeline log:
```
[deploy-bot] terraform apply interrupted: user_abort by maya at 1803002560
```

deploy-bot: Canary halted for `nodepool/gpu-training` in `us-west-2`. Rollout paused.

priya: OK, plan: 1) pin Helm aws-cni back to 1.3.2 in the gitops branch and merge small patch to revert change 2) update TF node_group launch template to prefer instance types with >=8 ENIs (or explicit instance selection) 3) run a small manual canary with 1 node and watch CNI attach metrics 4) if good, continue rollout.

jon: cost note: preferring larger instance types increases hourly cost; we should consider temporarily expanding IP pools (subnet size) in the VPC or moving to ENITrunking where possible to maximize IP capacity. Both have infra lead time.

rachel: I'll draft a one-off terraform change to the launch template constraints so mixed-instance won't pick the low-eni variants. Will push a branch and tag for review.

maya: pushed branch `tf/nodegroup-affinity-eni-fix` with a constraint: `allowed_instance_types = ["g5.xlarge","g5.2xlarge","p3.2xlarge"]` and test canary set to 1.

sam: after rachel's change we should do a manual node spin and validate `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and `kubectl logs -n kube-system aws-node` for attach errors for 15m. If green, let gitops finish.

priya: adding a follow-up task to the postmortem: separate helm addon upgrades from node launches in the pipeline so CNI changes don't coincide with capacity changes.

maya: agreed. Also adding a quick healthgate: check ENI capacity per instance type before allowing nodegroup update in pipeline.

jon: +1. Also let's add a cost/budget note in the rollout PR: if we temporarily enforce larger instances, include expected delta.

maya: thanks all — keeping this thread updated as we validate.

sam: 👍 keep an eye on autoscaler decisions too; it can be noisy when a few nodes start unschedulable.
